text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch central bank not to seek additional revenues for Dfl
100 million income loss due to introduction of smartcards. (p1)
- Dutch exports rise nine percent in 1996 Q3 year-on-year.
- Publisher Reed Elsevier trumps rival Wolters-Kluwer by taking over Colofon in an auction. (p1)
- Philips chief Pieter van der Wal has to resign as board chairman of Grundig. (p3)
- Dairy concern Campina considers relaunching its Mona product Vifit on the German market. (p3)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM is following cut-price airline EasyJet's price policy. (p3)
- Shareholders in utility concern UNA are opposing merger between four Dutch energy production companies. (p3)
- Brokerage firm Van der Moolen buys nine percent of its own shares. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen puts aside 100 million guilders to follow up on good ideas from farmers. (p2)
- Automation company Getronics enters into a pay and conditions agreement for the first time in its existence. (p2)
- Sale of state's interest in truck maker DAF to U.S. Paccar brought 154 million guilders. (p2)
- Supermarket chain Spar to open shops in Texaco filling
stations. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch C.I.D. suspects a number of prominent Dutchmen of involvement in criminal activities. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank to provide economic and financial news for customers having a GSM mobile phone. (p3)
- Chip Market Europe to continue its legal action against chemicals concern Akzo Nobel for stealing patent on solar cells. (p21)
- Robeco chief prof. dr. J.J. van Duyn forecasts a 10-15 pct
correction of the stock market in July. (p21)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics and Amsterdam Stadium Arena settle their conflict over rival Sony sponsoring a soccer tournament.
TROUW
- Amnesty International and Pax Christi very disappointed in Royal Dutch/Shell's new code of conduct. (p7)
- Investors react enthusiastically to ABN Amro bank's ships'
investment fund Norships CV. (p7)
